paper.title_en: Ultra-broadband quantum infrared spectroscopy extending to 20 µm
paper.abstract_en: Quantum infrared spectroscopy (QIRS), which exploits quantum interference between photon-pair generation processes, enables infrared spectroscopy using only visible and near-infrared (VNIR) light sources and detectors. Extending the spectral coverage of QIRS into the long-wavelength infrared region up to 20 µm is crucial for the identification and characterization of a broad range of materials. However, implementing QIRS beyond 10 µm has been challenging because the nonlinear materials used to date do not provide suitable photon-pair sources in this spectral region. Here, we design a wavelength-tunable photon-pair source based on a gallium selenide crystal and develop a QIRS system covering a broad spectral range from 8.6 to 20 µm. Using this system, we measure the transmittance spectrum of a polystyrene film and observe characteristic absorption bands beyond 10 µm relevant to identifying polystyrene and to probing local chain conformation. These results demonstrate that QIRS is capable of covering the entire molecular fingerprint region.
